text:
For a typical **120V electric blanket**, I’d look at the **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024Wh)**. It’s rated for about **12 hours with a 150W blanket** in one estimate, so it should cover an eight-hour night for many blankets that cycle on and off ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)). A smaller 300Wh station is unlikely to last the night.

**Important caveat:** runtime depends on the blanket’s actual average draw. If it pulls its full rated wattage continuously, a 1kWh station may not make eight hours; check the blanket’s label. For more buffer, a **roughly 2kWh station** is a safer choice—the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 is estimated at about 23 hours for the same 150W blanket ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)).

Plug the blanket directly into the station, and keep the station off the bed and away from the blanket’s folds ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night)).
